facts.scope: Scan-rescan repeatability of radiomic features from diffusion and perfusion MRI in glioblastoma

facts.scope: Functional and structural connectome prediction tasks
facts.subject_leakage_experiment: Duplicated the exact same scans for a fraction of participants before partitioning
facts.finding_used: Allowing duplicates across training and test partitions inflated prediction performance
facts.stated_design_limit: The duplicated-scan experiment is not directly comparable to longitudinal or repeated-measurement studies

studies.permitted_claim: The experiment illustrates a dependence-related leakage risk relevant to keeping all scans from a patient together
studies.limits: Does not quantify bias in our diagnostic task, establish that all leakage was eliminated, or validate our source annotation process. Do not describe identical-scan duplication as a real longitudinal glioma validation experiment.

own_study_claims.claim: One six-neighbor erosion on the supplied voxel grid retains the original image percentile and full-ROI discretization references
Eroded-minus-original Fusion AUC difference is 0.0062272963155163286; its conditional paired interval includes zero
All 20 within-partition Fusion-minus-M1 AUC differences are positive; the same cohort is reused
Original ROI and primary partition remain primary; repeated distributions are descriptive and do not replace the primary uncertainty interval

interpretations: A small observed change under one erosion suggests limited sensitivity to that particular perturbation, without demonstrating equivalence, segmentation accuracy or general robustness to all boundary changes
Twenty positive increments support directional consistency under the observed partitions, not independent replication or external validation
Neither check establishes acquisition repeatability, source-label validity or performance at other institutions
